threat_model: The attacker sees a release in which direct identifiers are replaced but PERSON pseudonyms are batch-consistent (policies.json: PERSON pseudonym_scope = batch), so documents about the same person can be linked. The attacker knows the registry (the outside world) and matches the quasi-identifiers visible across a person's linked documents against it. anonymity_set_size (k) is computed over the attributes as written in the source documents; anonymity_set_size_after_first_pass over only those still readable after the expected first-pass strategies (kept values, plus age bands, since generalising an age to a 10-year band preserves the band). expected_strategies are Agent 2's first-pass decisions under policies.json, before any Agent 4/5 remediation. A planted risk that is reidentifiable and survives_first_pass must be flagged by Agent 5; a control (k >= 3) must not be.

Job title and employer in the speaker bio, exact age in the award item. Quillon has two solutions architects; only one is 30-39.

Velloran has two events coordinators (Chennai and Kochi), both at the Coastal Finance Forum. Job title and employer in the personnel note; age 31 and Chennai, away from her name, in the leave request. Either the age band or the city separates them.

No name anywhere, yet 'the only assistant warden of the girls' hostel' at Kestrelmoor is one person. The document has three quasi-identifier types, so CTX-01 generalises them in the first pass; the risk is caught by policy rather than by linkage.

edge_cases.expected_behaviour: 'Dr. Ananya Rao', 'A. Rao', 'Dr. Rao' and 'Ananya Rao' are all T01. Agent 1 should cluster them as one entity so they receive one batch pseudonym.
'Ananya Rao' (T01) and 'Vikram Rao' (T02) share a surname but are different people. A surname match alone must not merge them or give them the same pseudonym.
rohan.mehta@example.com appears in both documents (T04). It links them in the raw text; it must be masked in both, which also breaks that link in the release.
No PERSON mention, but role + place + join date single out T03 (k = 1). CTX-01 should fire on the document and generalise the occupation, organisation, department and date.
Date of birth, postcode and gender in one document: CTX-03 raises all three to high, so the DOB is generalised and the postcode and gender masked; the SSN-like number is suppressed.
A diagnosis in a document that names the person (T07): CTX-05 raises it to critical, so it is suppressed, not just masked.
Nationality stated about a named person (T05) in the same sentence: CTX-06 raises it to high and it is masked.
'3 February 2025' and '12 January 2025' stand alone in their sentences and are about nobody. CTX-01 fires on both documents, but EXC-01 caps these dates at low, so they are kept.

Kavya Menon (T06) works from Chennai (registry) but news-004 says Kochi, where a different Velloran events coordinator (C29) is based. The conflict must not be resolved by merging her with C29 or by trusting either city; the Kochi mention is marked contradicts_registry.
A press release about an organisation that describes no person. Mentions have no person_id; the isolated date and location stay readable (EXC-01, EXC-02); there is nobody to re-identify.
